name: Mai Chau food guide
summary: Dinner in Mai Châu is the stilt-house table in Bản Lác or Pom Coọng. Cơm lam comes out of its bamboo tube, hill chicken comes off the charcoal with a dish of chẩm chéo, and jar wine sees out the evening. Up the valley, Bản Hịch and the Hmong village of Hang Kia cook plates of their own.
body: Eat Mai Châu at the homestay, not on a restaurant street. The valley table runs to grilled chicken, pork skewers with mắc khén, sticky rice, grass duck, sour bamboo, and the insect plates: fried cicadas, grilled crickets, and forest bee pupae. Bản Hịch, about 12 km from the old district center, has three dishes of its own, and Hang Kia adds upland sticky rice, village pig, grilled chicken, and bánh dày.

Thai houses also keep the slower dishes: buffalo hung for months in the kitchen smoke and eaten with rượu Mai Hạ, upland sticky rice steamed in a wooden steamer, and stream fish fried and served with a sharp, slightly bitter mustard soup. Some of these are not cooked every day, so ask your host ahead.
specialtiesLead: The homestay table first, then the Bản Hịch hamlet and Hang Kia. Two wines and a dipping sauce sit on the list with the plates.

sections.heading: On the homestay table
paragraphs: These are the plates, the two wines, and the dipping sauce cooked in the valley and its highland. Ask at the house for them.

spots.name: Bamboo sticky rice
spots.note: Sticky rice cooked inside a bamboo tube. Peel the tube back and dip the rice in minced peanuts.

spots.name: Hill chicken
spots.note: Native chicken that runs the hills, with firm meat. It comes grilled over charcoal without a smoky taste, or steamed with lime leaf, with chẩm chéo for dipping.

spots.name: Pork skewers
spots.note: Grilled pork skewers, one of the valley’s favourite homestay plates. Guests eat them with mắc khén beside sticky rice and grilled fish.

spots.name: Fried cicadas
spots.note: Cicadas, stuffed and fried, a local dish of the valley.

spots.name: Grass duck
spots.note: Grass duck, one of the plates families serve in the Mai Châu valley.

spots.name: Suckling pig
spots.note: Lợn cắp nách is one of the pork dishes on the valley table, served as its own plate beside lợn mán.

spots.name: Man pig
spots.note: Lợn mán is another of the valley’s pork dishes, served beside lợn cắp nách.

spots.name: Grilled chicken
spots.note: Grilled chicken, cooked on the valley table and in the Hmong village of Hang Kia.

spots.name: Grilled crickets
spots.note: Grilled crickets, one of the valley’s insect plates.

spots.name: Sticky rice
spots.note: Sticky rice that comes with the homestay meal in Pom Coọng and the Thai villages. Guests eat it with grilled fish and pork skewers with mắc khén.

spots.name: Jar wine
spots.note: Jar wine, brought out with the evening at the stilt house in Pom Coọng and across the valley.

spots.name: Mai Ha wine
spots.note: A Thai wine made with forest leaves, drunk alongside smoked buffalo.

spots.name: Forest bee pupae
spots.note: Pupae of forest bees, another of the valley’s insect plates.

spots.name: Sour bamboo
spots.note: Sour bamboo shoots from the valley table.

spots.name: Green-headed duck
spots.note: Green-headed duck, one of the three plates Bản Hịch cooks, about 12 km from the old district center.

spots.name: Sang greens
spots.note: Sắng greens, another of the three plates Bản Hịch cooks.

spots.name: Green pickled fish
spots.note: Green pickled fish, the last of the three plates Bản Hịch cooks.

spots.name: Upland sticky rice
spots.note: Upland sticky rice that Thai families steam in a wooden steamer, a guest dish worth asking for ahead. Eat it with sesame salt, grilled village pork, or grilled hill chicken.

spots.name: Village pig
spots.note: Village pig, cooked at Hang Kia and grilled beside the sticky rice in Thai houses.

spots.name: Banh day
spots.note: A rice cake served among the Hmong-village dishes of Hang Kia.

spots.name: Stream fish
spots.note: Small stream fish such as goby and snakehead, fried or grilled and eaten bones and all. It is not on the table every day, so ask the house.

spots.name: Fried stream fish
spots.note: The fried plate of stream fish, served with Hmong mustard soup in Thai houses.

spots.name: Hmong mustard soup
spots.note: A northwest mustard-green soup with a sharp, slightly bitter taste, served beside fried stream fish.

spots.name: Smoked buffalo
spots.note: Buffalo loin and shoulder seasoned with lemongrass, ginger, garlic, dried chili, and mắc khén, then hung in the kitchen smoke for months. A good piece stays a little red, and it goes with rượu Mai Hạ.

spots.name: Cham cheo
spots.note: A dipping sauce of northwest seasonings, served with hill chicken.

sections.heading: Markets
paragraphs: The everyday meal is still the house. Three markets keep different days.

spots.name: Sunday morning market
spots.note: On Sunday morning people arrive in formal dress, and it is the morning woven cloth is sold. It is a different market from Pà Cò.

spots.name: Pa Co market
spots.note: The Pà Cò market meets on Sunday morning, and Bản Chà Đáy holds a night market on Saturday evening. The highland is about 30 km from the old township on National Highway 6 toward Sơn La.

spots.name: Ban Lac Saturday night market
spots.nameVi: Chợ đêm văn hóa Bản Lác
spots.note: A cultural night market runs at Bản Lác, in xã Mai Hạ, on Saturday evening.

seoTitle: Mai Chau food guide — dinner at the stilt-house table
seoDescription: Dinner is the stilt house: bamboo-tube rice, hill chicken with chẩm chéo, pork skewers, and jar wine. Bản Hịch and Hang Kia add plates of their own.
